questions.q: Let $x = sin\left(2\tan^{- 1}\alpha\right)$ and $y = sin\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\tan^{- 1}\dfrac{4}{3}\right)$. If $S = \left\{\alpha \in \mathbb{R}: {y}^{2} = 1 - x\right\}$, then $\mathop{∑}_{\alpha \in S}16{\alpha}^{3}$ is equal to _______.
questions.solution:
Given $x = sin\left(2\tan^{- 1}\alpha\right) = sin\left(\tan^{- 1}\dfrac{2\alpha}{1 - {\alpha}^{2}}\right) = sin\left(\sin^{- 1}\dfrac{2\alpha}{1 + {\alpha}^{2}}\right) = \dfrac{2\alpha}{1 + {\alpha}^{2}} ⋯ \left(i\right)$

and $y = sin\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\tan^{- 1}\dfrac{4}{3}\right) = sin\left(\tan^{- 1}\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = sin\left(\sin^{- 1}\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\right) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{5}} . . . \left(ii\right)$

Now, ${y}^{2} = 1 - x$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{5} = 1 - \dfrac{2\alpha}{1 + {\alpha}^{2}}$ (from $\left(i\right) \text{ and } \left(ii\right)$)

$⇒ 1 + {\alpha}^{2} = 5 + 5{\alpha}^{2} - 10\alpha$

$⇒ 2{\alpha}^{2} - 5\alpha + 2 = 0$

$∴ \alpha = 2, \dfrac{1}{2}$

$∴ \mathop{∑}_{\alpha \in S}16{\alpha}^{3} = 16 \times {2}^{3} + 16 \times \dfrac{1}{{2}^{3}} = 16\left(\dfrac{65}{8}\right)$

$= 130$

questions.solution:
We have, $\sin^{2}10 ° \times sin20 ° \times sin40 ° \times sin50 ° \times sin70 °$

$= \left(sin10 ° \times sin50 ° \times sin70 °\right)\left(sin10 ° \times sin20 ° \times sin40 °\right)$

Using, $sin\theta = cos\left(90 ° - \theta\right)$

$= \left[cos80 ° \times cos40 ° \times cos20 °\right]\left[sin10 ° \times sin\left(30 ° - 10 °\right) \times sin\left(30 ° + 10 °\right)\right]$

We know that $cos\thetacos2\thetacos{2}^{2}\theta \ldots cos{2}^{n - 1}\theta = \dfrac{sin{2}^{n}\theta}{{2}^{n}sin\theta}$

and $sin\left(A + B\right) \cdot sin\left(A - B\right) = \sin^{2}A - \sin^{2}B$$⇒ \left(\dfrac{sin{2}^{3}\left(20 °\right)}{{2}^{3}sin20 °}\right)\left[sin10 ° \times \left(\dfrac{1}{4} - \sin^{2}10 °\right)\right]$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{sin160 °}{{2}^{3}sin20 °}\right)\left(\dfrac{sin10 ° - 4\sin^{3}10 °}{4}\right)$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{sin\left(180 ° - 20 °\right)}{8sin20 °}\right)\left(\dfrac{3sin10 ° - 4\sin^{3}10 ° - 2sin10 °}{4}\right)$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{sin20 °}{8sin20 °}\right)\left(\dfrac{sin30 ° - 2sin10 °}{4}\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{8}\left(\dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2} - 2sin10 °}{4}\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{8}\left(\dfrac{1 - 4sin10 °}{8}\right) = \alpha - \dfrac{sin10 °}{16}$ (given)

$⇒ \dfrac{1 - 4sin10 °}{64} = \dfrac{16\alpha - sin10 °}{16}$

$⇒ 1 - 4sin10 ° = 64\alpha - 4sin10 °$

$⇒ \alpha = \dfrac{1}{64}$.

questions.question: If $\sin^{2}\left(10 °\right)sin\left(20 °\right)sin\left(40 °\right)sin\left(50 °\right)sin\left(70 °\right) = \alpha -$ $\dfrac{1}{16}sin\left(10 °\right)$, then $16 + {\alpha}^{- 1}$ is equal to _____.
questions.explanation:
We have, $\sin^{2}10 ° \times sin20 ° \times sin40 ° \times sin50 ° \times sin70 °$

$= \left(sin10 ° \times sin50 ° \times sin70 °\right)\left(sin10 ° \times sin20 ° \times sin40 °\right)$

Using, $sin\theta = cos\left(90 ° - \theta\right)$

$= \left[cos80 ° \times cos40 ° \times cos20 °\right]\left[sin10 ° \times sin\left(30 ° - 10 °\right) \times sin\left(30 ° + 10 °\right)\right]$

We know that $cos\thetacos2\thetacos{2}^{2}\theta \ldots cos{2}^{n - 1}\theta = \dfrac{sin{2}^{n}\theta}{{2}^{n}sin\theta}$

and $sin\left(A + B\right) \cdot sin\left(A - B\right) = \sin^{2}A - \sin^{2}B$$⇒ \left(\dfrac{sin{2}^{3}\left(20 °\right)}{{2}^{3}sin20 °}\right)\left[sin10 ° \times \left(\dfrac{1}{4} - \sin^{2}10 °\right)\right]$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{sin160 °}{{2}^{3}sin20 °}\right)\left(\dfrac{sin10 ° - 4\sin^{3}10 °}{4}\right)$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{sin\left(180 ° - 20 °\right)}{8sin20 °}\right)\left(\dfrac{3sin10 ° - 4\sin^{3}10 ° - 2sin10 °}{4}\right)$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{sin20 °}{8sin20 °}\right)\left(\dfrac{sin30 ° - 2sin10 °}{4}\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{8}\left(\dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2} - 2sin10 °}{4}\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{8}\left(\dfrac{1 - 4sin10 °}{8}\right) = \alpha - \dfrac{sin10 °}{16}$ (given)

$⇒ \dfrac{1 - 4sin10 °}{64} = \dfrac{16\alpha - sin10 °}{16}$

$⇒ 1 - 4sin10 ° = 64\alpha - 4sin10 °$

$⇒ \alpha = \dfrac{1}{64}$.

questions.q: The number of integral values of $k$ for which the equation $3sinx + 4cosx = k + 1$ has a solution, $k \in R$ is _______.
questions.solution:
$3sinx + 4cosx = k + 1$

$⇒ k + 1 \in \left[- \sqrt{{3}^{2} + {4}^{2}}, \sqrt{{3}^{2} + {4}^{2}}\right]$

$⇒ k + 1 \in \left[- 5, 5\right]$

$⇒ k \in \left[- 6, 4\right]$

No. of integral values of $k = 11$
